deals.headline: Lerner family ends exploration of a Nationals sale
deals.summary: The Lerner family began exploring a sale in 2022; on 19 February 2024 Mark Lerner said the family will not sell the team. No transaction.

name: Washington Nationals
notes: Revenue, player expenses and operating income (EBITDA, net of revenue sharing and stadium debt service) are Forbes estimates for the 2025 season; Forbes puts debt/value at 26%. Founded left null: the franchise began as the Montreal Expos (Forbes: in Washington since 2005), and the only page read giving a year (MLB stats API firstYearOfPlay '1968') is the expansion award year, not a first season, so it was not used. Forbes lists the 2006 price paid as $450M; no page read gives individual family members' stakes (other principal owners include sons-in-law Robert Tanenbaum and Edward Cohen per AP, not verified on a fetched page). SBJ reports the team leaving MASN for MLB's local media; Forbes lists 'tv: MLB Local Media'; no media-rights deal recorded. Legal entity, kit/sponsor and social counts not found.

owners.evidence: Mark has served as one of the principal owners of the Nationals since the Lerner family purchased the team in July 2006.
owners.name: Mark D. Lerner

ownership_summary: Owned by the Lerner family, which bought the club from MLB in July 2006 (Forbes: price paid $450M). Mark D. Lerner has been managing principal owner and MLB control person since June 2018, succeeding his father Ted Lerner. The family explored a sale from April 2022 and ended the process in February 2024.

stadium_owner.detail: Owned by Events DC / the District of Columbia.
